cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel, a song for the dedication of the temple. David's talking straight to the LORD, and he opens with, "I will exalt You, O LORD," because the LORD lifted him up. Friend, NOBODY appreciates getting lifted up like a stamper who spent years in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: The LORD lifted David up. What does David say the LORD didn't let his foes do?

cards.text: Then David tells how it went down. Not a polite little text, friend, he CRIED to the LORD for help.

cards.question: David cried to the LORD for help, and the LORD ___ him.

cards.text: And this was no paper cut, friend. David says the LORD pulled him up from Sheol and spared him from going down into the Pit.

cards.question: True or false: By Sheol and the Pit, David means he came close to dying.

cards.text: Then David turns to everybody else and calls them in: "Sing to the LORD, O you His saints, and praise His holy name." He went from crying for help to LEADING THE CHOIR.

cards.question: David puts the LORD's anger side by side with His favor. What does he say about His anger?

answers.text: It's fleeting next to His favor
It falls only on His foes

cards.question: David has another line for the saints: "Weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning." True or false: he means sorrow won't last forever and joy is on its way.

cards.text: Now David gets honest about himself. There was a time he said, "I will never be shaken."

cards.question: David once said, "I will never be shaken." When does he say he talked like that?

cards.text: Back then, the LORD had favored him and made his mountain stand strong. I felt that solid on my old kitchen counter too, right up until a SHINY new stamper showed up.

cards.question: When the LORD hid His face, David was ___.

cards.text: So David calls to the LORD and begs for mercy. Then he makes his case like it's closing arguments.

cards.question: David asks the LORD, "Will the dust praise You?" What's his point?

answers.text: If he dies he can't praise the LORD
Even dust will praise the LORD someday
His foes are worth no more than dust

cards.text: Then David boils it all down: hear me, have mercy, be my helper. No fancy speech this time, friend, just HELP.
And David says the LORD turned his mourning into DANCING. Friend, when good news hits me, I'm hopping around on this gold base like the oven timer just went off.

cards.question: The LORD peeled off David's sackcloth and clothed him with ___.
Why does David say the LORD clothed him with joy?

answers.text: So his heart would sing and not be silent
So his foes would see it and be ashamed
So the people would follow him to battle

cards.question: David closes with a promise to the LORD. True or false: he says he'll give thanks until his troubles are over.

findings.problem: The joke says Papa Dorin felt solid on the counter 'right up until a SHINY new stamper showed up.' His backstory says the opposite. Before the new stamper came, he was already worn down, his stamps were blurry, and he watched every new box come in knowing 'It was only a matter of time.' The joke changes his story instead of telling it as written.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the exact word in Psalm 30:7. 'Dismayed', 'ashamed' and 'angry' are all reasonable feelings for someone when the LORD hides His face, so the baker can't reason it out from card 12 and is guessing wording they haven't seen. 'Dismayed' also sounds more like Bible language than the other two, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
